header: Words of a question that no document has. The circular search treats a word found in no circular as noise (a typo, a synonym: tokenWeights.ts gives it weight 0). That is right for the ranking, but it means that "LTC rules" quietly becomes "rules" and returns whatever has the word "rules", with a percentage. Under the "Circulars & Notices" choice the reader asked for documents only, so I make the bar say what is true: that no circular, notice or announcement has the word. When most of the question's words are absent, I show nothing (nothing in the archive is about it); when only one of several is absent, the results stand with a one-line note. I use this only under that choice: "Everything" keeps the old behaviour.

symbols.name: absentWords
symbols.sig: export async function absentWords(ds: DataSource, words: string[]): Promise<string[]>
doc: Returns the words (of those given) that appear in NO circular (its text or its headline), announcement (its title, its text, its PDF's text); [] when the lookup fails, because then I claim nothing.

members.name: nothing
doc: Most of the question is in no document, so I show nothing but the sentence.

members.name: partial
doc: Some word is in no document but the rest is, so I show the results with the sentence above them.

symbols.name: judgeAbsent
symbols.sig: export function judgeAbsent(contentWords: string[], absent: string[]): AbsentVerdict
doc: Pure: works out what to say, from the question's content words and those that no document has.

behaviours: 'ltc rules': half the words are in no document -> nothing is shown, the sentence names LTC
one word of three is in no document -> the results stay, with a note
every word is somewhere -> nothing is said
two absent words of two -> nothing is shown, both are named
no words, or no absent word, is quiet and never throws
absentWords names the words that are nowhere
a word asked again within ten minutes is not asked of the database again
words shorter than three letters are never judged
when the lookup fails nothing is claimed (the search goes on as it always did)
a percent or underscore in a word cannot widen the pattern
